welcome.label: Welcome · Magnet Fishing Day

parts.label: 🎣 Magnet fishing
parts.title: Cleanup day at the pond
parts.body: Five things fell off the dock after the Duck Derby.

parts.label: 🧲 The magnet kit
parts.title: The magnets push apart!
parts.body: How should the team stack them?

welcome.script:
(Hold a fridge magnet up to a metal spoon or a paperclip.) Click! Now watch. (Hold it to a soda can.) Nothing. Hmm.

[ON SCREEN: Magnet fishing]
The Duck Derby is over, and the pond needs a cleanup. Dr. Nair’s team has a magnet on a rope and a long net.

[ON SCREEN: The lost-item log]
Five things fell off the dock. Some come up on the magnet. Some need the net.

[ON SCREEN: The magnet kit]
And their two magnets keep pushing each other away! Read the case file just below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · cast and reel (Clue 1)

parts.label: 🎣 Cast and reel
parts.title: Six muddy shapes
rows: Drag the magnet onto a shape

parts.label: 📝 The haul
parts.title: What clanked on?
parts.body: What do the things that came up have in common?

warmup.script:
(Pretend to drop a rope over the side of your desk, then pull it up slowly.) Got something… I think!

[ON SCREEN: Cast and reel]
Drag the magnet onto a muddy shape on the pond bottom. Make your guess, Clank or Nothing, then reel it up. Six casts.

[ON SCREEN: The haul]
Watch your haul list. Some metal things come up, and some metal things stay in the mud. Why? Answer the question, and Clue one is yours.

part1.label: Part 1 · the worn-label magnet (Clue 2)

parts.label: 💥 Snap it
parts.title: One N piece and one S piece?
parts.body: Test the two new ends and see.

part1.script:
(Hold two fridge magnets back to back, then flip one so they snap together.) Push… flip… snap!

[ON SCREEN: The rule]
Opposite poles pull together. Same poles push apart.

[ON SCREEN: The worn-label magnet]
This magnet’s letters wore off. Use the test magnet to find out which end is N and which is S. Then paint them.

[ON SCREEN: Snap it]
Then snap it in half. Do you get an N piece and an S piece? Test the new ends and find out.

part2.label: Part 2 · the magnet sweeper (Clue 3)
part2.script:
(Hold up a key and a paperclip.) Both metal. Will a magnet grab both?

[ON SCREEN: The sweeper]
Drag the magnet wand slowly over the tray. Watch what jumps up and what stays put. Read every made-of tag.

part3.label: Part 2 · the iron filings photo
part3.script:
(Wave your hand slowly around an imaginary magnet.) A magnet’s pull is invisible. But we can see it.

[ON SCREEN: The filings]
This real photo is more than 100 years old. Tiny bits of iron lined up around a magnet. Tap each number to find where the pull is strongest, and where it is weakest.

explore.label: Part 4 · the prediction chart (Clue 4)

parts.label: 📋 The chart
parts.title: Predict EVERY row first
rows: Yes or No for all eight

parts.label: ⭕ Circled
parts.title: Circled = something new
parts.body: A wrong prediction shows you what you didn’t know yet.

explore.script:
(Hold up a coin.) This is a nickel. Is a nickel magnetic? Don’t answer yet!

[ON SCREEN: The chart]
In Part 4, predict every row first, Yes or No, for all eight things. Lock your chart. Then drag the magnet onto each row.

[ON SCREEN: Circled]
Wrong guesses get circled. Good! That’s where the learning is. Then finish the rule. That’s Clue four.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: Magnet or net?
parts.body: Check each lost item’s made-of line. And fix the magnet kit.

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
Use all four clues. Which lost things come up on the magnet, which need the net, and how do you stack the magnets? Then stamp the ranger’s report and open the tackle box!

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Next, two short answers. For Part C, plan two magnets near each other, then sketch and label every pole. Last comes your CER.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
(Pretend to stick a magnet on everything around you: the desk leg, a window, a can.) It sticks to everything metal… right?

[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A classmate says magnets stick to all metal. You tested lots of metals today.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side and two facts. Then explain how they prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…”

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🎣 Your specimen
parts.title: The rusty bolt from the pond
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: 🧭 The compass
parts.title: A compass is a magnet too

parts.label: ➡ Next lesson
parts.title: A real fair test
parts.body: Test magnets like a scientist, with a data table.

closing.script:
(Hold up an imaginary rusty bolt like a trophy.) The pond is clean!

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and the rusty bolt goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: The compass]
Did you catch the twist? A compass needle is a tiny magnet, and Earth is a giant one.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next lesson]
Next lesson: a real fair test of magnets, with a data table.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
